profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Ashburn VA3, is located at 44245 Gigabit Plaza, Ashburn, VA 20147, the third of nine planned buildings on NTT's 224-megawatt, 78-acre Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley." The operator publishes 112,000 square feet of data floor space and 16 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; no formal certifications or opening year are stated on the page.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027; regulators approved $775.6 million of the roughly $1.2 billion Dominion sought, cutting about $350 million tied to speculative data center projects, according to Inside Climate News. Under the new rules, data center customers with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold NTT's Ashburn campus far exceeds, must sign 14-year mandatory contracts, pay a minimum 85% of transmission and distribution costs and a minimum 60% of generation costs regardless of actual usage, and post collateral upfront for grid upgrades; the Piedmont Environmental Council has criticized the deal, noting an estimated 61% of grid-upgrade costs still fall on ordinary ratepayers once a facility's contract term ends.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT VA3 publishes 16 MW of IT capacity, ranking sixteenth among nineteen Virginia facilities that disclose a megawatt figure and representing roughly 1.2 percent of the state's published total.

At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 16 MW of IT load spans roughly 1,600 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density more typical of GPU training clusters, the same 16 MW supports roughly 400 racks. At 700 W per H100, 400 racks at that density would hold on the order of 22,800 accelerators. These are assumptions about rack density, not NTT's published claims, and the operator does not state a rack count or supported workload type on the facility page this site read.

Ashburn is the densest data center corridor in Virginia and one of the most interconnected in the world. The published specifications for VA3 do not include certifications, interconnection depth, or available fiber. At 16 MW, VA3 is a mid-small facility in its state context, relevant to colocation buyers but not, on published figures alone, a facility that moves the needle on AI scaling at the regional level. Virginia hosts 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the overwhelming majority publish no capacity figure at all, so the state total is a floor, not a ceiling.
